# How to Use Google’s Built-In AI to Organise Your Daily Life

Imagine opening your laptop on a busy Monday morning, staring at a mountain of unread emails, and wishing someone could just summarise the chaos for you. With the latest updates to the online tools you already use every day, that helpful assistant is now sitting right inside your screen, ready to help you sort through the noise.

Instead of copying and pasting text back and forth between different apps, you can now use built-in AI helpers directly inside Gmail, Google Docs, and Google Sheets. Here is how to get started with these tools to make your daily life and work feel a lot lighter.

## Working smarter inside your inbox

Most of us spend far too much time wading through long email threads trying to find a single piece of information. The latest update introduces a smart sidebar panel (the small sliding window on the right side of your screen where the AI helper lives) that can read and analyse your emails.

To use it, you simply open a long email thread and click the little sparkle icon in the top right corner. You can type a prompt (the text instruction you give to the AI) asking it to find specific details. 

For example, you could ask: 
* *"What time did Sarah say we should meet, and what did she ask me to bring?"*
* *"Summarise this thread into three bullet points."*

The AI will scan the entire conversation and give you a neat, friendly summary in seconds, saving you from scrolling through weeks of replies.

## Planning and creating in Google Docs

When you are staring at a blank page trying to write a newsletter, a family budget, or a work proposal, getting started is often the hardest part. The built-in AI in Google Docs can now help you draft content based on files you already have stored in your Google Drive.

This works because the system is multimodal (meaning it is an AI that can understand and connect different types of information, like text, images, and spreadsheets, all at the same time). 

If you are planning a family holiday, you can open a new Google Doc, click the AI helper, and ask it to look at a travel spreadsheet in your Drive to create a daily itinerary. It does the heavy lifting of reading your notes and organising them into a beautifully formatted document, leaving you with more time to actually look forward to your trip.

## What this means for you

Integrating smart assistants directly into your daily apps makes technology feel less like a chore and more like a helpful partner.

* **For your personal life**: Use the email summary tool to quickly find school permission slips, party details, or utility bills without endless searching. You can also use Docs to draft polite emails to landlords or plan weekly family meal schedules.
* **For your business or work**: You can extract key action items from long client threads instantly. Instead of writing meeting minutes from scratch, let the AI read your rough notes and format them into a professional email ready to send to your team.
* **If you're just getting started**: Don't feel pressured to use it for everything. Start small. The next time you get an email that is longer than three paragraphs, click the sparkle icon in Gmail and ask it to summarise the message for you.

## Wrap-up

Having an AI assistant built directly into your daily workspace means you no longer need to be a technology expert to save time on your daily chores. By letting the helper summarise long threads and draft quick outlines, you can clear the digital clutter and focus on what really matters. Open your Gmail account today, look for that little sparkle icon in the top corner, and ask it to help you tackle your very next email.
